from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    base = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    row_marks = [r for r in range(h) if base not in grid[r]]
    col_marks = [c for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c] != base for r in range(h))]

    separator_bg = Counter(
        v for row in grid for v in row if v != base
    ).most_common(1)[0][0]

    out = []
    for i in range(len(row_marks) - 1):
        row = []
        for j in range(len(col_marks) - 1):
            corners = [
                grid[row_marks[i]][col_marks[j]],
                grid[row_marks[i]][col_marks[j + 1]],
                grid[row_marks[i + 1]][col_marks[j]],
                grid[row_marks[i + 1]][col_marks[j + 1]],
            ]
            if corners.count(corners[0]) == 4 and corners[0] != separator_bg:
                row.append(corners[0])
            else:
                row.append(base)
        out.append(row)
    return out

from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    background = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]

    row_lines = [r for r in range(h)
                 if grid[r].count(background) > w / 2]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w)
                 if sum(grid[r][c] == background for r in range(h)) > h / 2]

    # Ignore an outer frame line; the encoded grid lies inside it.
    row_lines = [r for r in row_lines if r not in (0, h - 1)]
    col_lines = [c for c in col_lines if c not in (0, w - 1)]

    # Restore boundary lines when they are part of the regular lattice.
    if h > 1 and grid[0].count(background) > w / 2:
        row_lines = [0] + row_lines
    if h > 1 and grid[-1].count(background) > w / 2:
        row_lines.append(h - 1)
    if w > 1 and sum(grid[r][0] == background for r in range(h)) > h / 2:
        col_lines = [0] + col_lines
    if w > 1 and sum(grid[r][-1] == background for r in range(h)) > h / 2:
        col_lines.append(w - 1)

    row_lines.sort()
    col_lines.sort()

    # The cell color is the most common color away from the separator lines.
    inner = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) if r not in row_lines
             for c in range(w) if c not in col_lines]
    fill = Counter(inner).most_common(1)[0][0]

    out = [[fill for _ in range(len(col_lines) - 1)]
           for _ in range(len(row_lines) - 1)]

    for i in range(len(row_lines) - 1):
        for j in range(len(col_lines) - 1):
            r1, r2 = row_lines[i], row_lines[i + 1]
            c1, c2 = col_lines[j], col_lines[j + 1]
            marks = []

            # Matching endpoint markers on any of the cell's four edges.
            for r in (r1, r2):
                a, b = grid[r][c1], grid[r][c2]
                if a == b and a not in (background, fill):
                    marks.append(a)
            for c in (c1, c2):
                a, b = grid[r1][c], grid[r2][c]
                if a == b and a not in (background, fill):
                    marks.append(a)

            if marks and all(x == marks[0] for x in marks):
                out[i][j] = marks[0]

    return out

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    colors = set(v for row in grid for v in row)

    # Grid separators form mostly-uniform horizontal and vertical lines.
    best = None
    for color in colors:
        rs = [r for r in range(h) if grid[r].count(color) > w * 0.55]
        cs = [c for c in range(w)
              if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) > h * 0.55]
        score = len(rs) + len(cs)
        if best is None or score > best[0]:
            best = (score, color, rs, cs)

    separator, rows, cols = best[1], best[2], best[3]

    # The leftmost full separator can be an outside frame rather than a grid edge.
    if cols and cols[0] == 0:
        cols = cols[1:]

    if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
        return []

    row_set, col_set = set(rows), set(cols)
    interior = [
        grid[r][c]
        for r in range(h) if r not in row_set
        for c in range(w) if c not in col_set
    ]
    fill = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]

    out = [[fill for _ in range(len(cols) - 1)]
           for _ in range(len(rows) - 1)]

    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            corners = [
                grid[rows[i]][cols[j]],
                grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]],
                grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]],
            ]
            if corners[0] != separator and corners.count(corners[0]) == 4:
                out[i][j] = corners[0]

    return out

from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    # Identify the repeated separator color from highly uniform rows and columns.
    dominant = []
    for row in grid:
        color, count = Counter(row).most_common(1)[0]
        if count / w >= 0.55:
            dominant.append(color)
    for c in range(w):
        color, count = Counter(grid[r][c] for r in range(h)).most_common(1)[0]
        if count / h >= 0.55:
            dominant.append(color)
    separator = Counter(dominant).most_common(1)[0][0]

    row_lines = [r for r in range(h)
                 if sum(v == separator for v in grid[r]) > w / 2]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w)
                 if sum(grid[r][c] == separator for r in range(h)) > h / 2]

    # A full separator at the far left is an outside frame.
    if col_lines and col_lines[0] == 0:
        col_lines = col_lines[1:]

    row_set, col_set = set(row_lines), set(col_lines)
    interior = [
        grid[r][c]
        for r in range(h) if r not in row_set
        for c in range(w) if c not in col_set
    ]
    fill = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]

    out = [[fill for _ in range(len(col_lines) - 1)]
           for _ in range(len(row_lines) - 1)]

    # A cell is marked when its top and bottom edges both carry a matching
    # pair of endpoint markers.
    for i in range(len(row_lines) - 1):
        top, bottom = row_lines[i], row_lines[i + 1]
        for j in range(len(col_lines) - 1):
            left, right = col_lines[j], col_lines[j + 1]

            a, b = grid[top][left], grid[top][right]
            c, d = grid[bottom][left], grid[bottom][right]

            if (a == b == c == d) and a not in (separator, fill):
                out[i][j] = a

    return out

from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    colors = set(v for row in grid for v in row)
    candidates = []

    for sep in colors:
        rows = [r for r in range(h)
                if grid[r].count(sep) >= 0.70 * w]
        cols = [c for c in range(w)
                if sum(grid[r][c] == sep for r in range(h)) >= 0.70 * h]

        if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
            continue
        if any(b - a < 2 for a, b in zip(rows, rows[1:])):
            continue
        if any(b - a < 2 for a, b in zip(cols, cols[1:])):
            continue

        def regularity(lines):
            gaps = [b - a for a, b in zip(lines, lines[1:])]
            return max(gaps) - min(gaps) if gaps else 999

        # Prefer the repeated, evenly spaced separator lattice.
        score = (regularity(rows) + regularity(cols),
                 -(len(rows) + len(cols)))
        candidates.append((score, sep, rows, cols))

    if not candidates:
        return grid

    _, sep, rows, cols = min(candidates, key=lambda x: x[0])

    # Ignore an outer frame rail if present.
    if cols and cols[0] == 0:
        cols = cols[1:]

    row_set, col_set = set(rows), set(cols)
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) if r not in row_set
                for c in range(w) if c not in col_set]
    fill = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]

    out = [[fill for _ in range(len(cols) - 1)]
           for _ in range(len(rows) - 1)]

    # Paired markers on each horizontal grid line color the cell below it.
    for i, r in enumerate(rows[:-1]):
        for j, (c1, c2) in enumerate(zip(cols, cols[1:])):
            a, b = grid[r][c1], grid[r][c2]
            if a == b and a not in (sep, fill):
                out[i][j] = a

    return out

from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    base = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Separator rows/columns are mostly the background color.
    row_candidates = [
        r for r in range(h)
        if sum(v == base for v in grid[r]) > w * 0.6
    ]
    col_candidates = [
        c for c in range(w)
        if sum(grid[r][c] == base for r in range(h)) > h * 0.6
    ]

    # Marker-bearing separator lines define the lattice; plain terminal
    # separator lines are inferred from its regular spacing.
    rows = [r for r in row_candidates
            if any(grid[r][c] != base for c in range(w))]
    cols = [c for c in col_candidates
            if any(grid[r][c] != base for r in range(h))]

    def extend(lines, candidates, limit):
        if len(lines) < 2:
            return lines
        gaps = [b - a for a, b in zip(lines, lines[1:])]
        step = Counter(gaps).most_common(1)[0][0]
        result = list(lines)
        nxt = result[-1] + step
        if nxt < limit and nxt in candidates:
            result.append(nxt)
        return result

    rows = extend(rows, row_candidates, h)
    cols = extend(cols, col_candidates, w)

    if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
        return grid

    line_rows, line_cols = set(rows), set(cols)
    inner = [
        grid[r][c]
        for r in range(h) if r not in line_rows
        for c in range(w) if c not in line_cols
    ]
    fill = Counter(inner).most_common(1)[0][0]

    out = [[fill for _ in range(len(cols) - 1)]
           for _ in range(len(rows) - 1)]

    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            corners = (
                grid[rows[i]][cols[j]],
                grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]],
                grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]],
            )
            if corners[0] != base and corners.count(corners[0]) == 4:
                out[i][j] = corners[0]

    return out
